stats-significance-effect.alt: Two panels, each with two overlapping bell curves: a control group and a treatment group. Left, a small effect: the means are 0.2 standard deviations apart and the curves overlap almost completely. Right, a large effect: the means are 0.8 standard deviations apart and the curves overlap less. A note says that with a large enough sample even the small effect can be statistically significant, because significance is not size.
